items.title: Decoding the microbiota–gut–brain axis in Parkinson’s disease: from microbial dysbiosis to systems-level regulation and acupuncture-based modulation
items.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a multisystem disorder involving dysfunction of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA), encompassing gut microbial dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolism, intestinal barrier impairment, immune dysregulation, autonomic dysfunction, and α-synuclein pathology. Sequencing studies identify PD-associated differences in microbial functional potential, whereas chemical measurements reveal changes in fecal SCFAs, bile acids in plasma or intestinal tissue, and tryptophan-derived metabolites in plasma or cerebrospinal fluid. These changes interact with intestinal barrier dysfunction, TLR4/NF-κB and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling, microglial activation, and neural pathways including the enteric and vagal systems, forming interconnected microbiota–metabolic–immune–neural feedback networks. We propose a systems framework in which pathological attractors, network collapse, and system reset denote testable hypotheses about persistent MGBA configurations, impaired functional recovery, and sustained changes in responses after intervention, respectively. Their evaluation requires longitudinal measurements, controlled perturbations, and comparison with alternative explanations; these concepts are not presented as established mechanisms of PD. Within this framework, acupuncture is considered a candidate intervention affecting several MGBA-related processes. Studies in PD models report concurrent changes in microbial composition, intestinal barrier markers, inflammatory signaling, and neurological outcomes, while microbiota-depletion and transplantation experiments provide initial support for a microbial contribution to selected treatment effects. However, these findings do not establish a complete acupuncture–MGBA–PD causal pathway. Human evidence remains preliminary and concerns symptomatic outcomes rather than demonstrated neuroprotection or disease modification. Restoration of MGBA homeostasis is therefore a hypothesis to be evaluated through prespecified measures of sustained physiological function and recovery after perturbation. We therefore propose a causal and state-oriented framework integrating longitudinal multi-omics, mechanistic perturbation, interpretable artificial intelligence, and biologically informed patient stratification. This framework may facilitate the transition from descriptive MGBA associations toward testable causal models and ultimately support the development of state-informed precision acupuncture strategies for PD.

items.title: Designing AI at the Rural Edge: A Micro-Social Venture Framework for Community-Led Digital Innovation
items.abstract: Generative and other AI-enabled technologies are accessible to small organisations, yet human–AI interaction (HAI) design guidance focuses on relatively direct user–system interaction. Rural HCI, community-centred design, participatory AI, digital inclusion, and social-enterprise research show that AI use is socially and organisationally situated. This late-breaking work develops the Micro-Social Venture (MSV) Framework through integrative conceptual synthesis of 55 selected sources. The framework connects six dimensions: Place, Community Agency, Organisational Mediation, Digital and AI Capability, Resource Conditions, and Governance and Social Outcomes. Its distinctive contribution is to treat the social venture as part of HAI itself: a community-embedded socio-technical intermediary through which AI is encountered, adapted, governed, and potentially refused. Five design propositions address place, collective agency, resource asymmetry, negotiated trust, and community stewardship. The framework is generative rather than predictive, offering HCI a diagnostic lens for examining community-embedded AI at geographic, organisational, infrastructural, and participatory edges.

items.title: DESIGNING AI-RESISTANT TASKS AS A TOOL FOR ASSESSING THE ANALYTICAL AND CRITICAL COMPETENCIES OF FUTURE TEACHERS
items.abstract: This article provides a theoretical foundation for assessing the analytical and critical competencies of future teachers in the era of generative artificial intelligence. It has been demonstrated that the limited reliability of automated AI-detection tools necessitates a shift from evaluating the final written product to a "process-over-product" diagnostic paradigm, while upholding the principles of academic integrity. Within the structure of an educator's analytical - critical competencies, the cognitive-diagnostic, didactic-design and reflexive-metacognitive components have been distinguished. A didactic model has been developed for designing AI - resistant assignments that focus on higher-order thinking skills, specifically "Analyzing", "Evaluating" and ″Creating″ according to Bloom's Taxonomy. The model incorporates the ″Three Zones ″ framework and utilizes three diagnostic formats: the analysis of contradictory pedagogical cases (Case Study), the cognitive auditing of AI-generated content (Reverse Engineering), and in-person, dialogue-based defense using the Socratic method (Socratic Defense). Furthermore, a criterion - based, multi-level rubric has been proposed comprising verification-analytical, didactic-adaptive, and metacognitive-authorial criteria to objectively assess students' professional agency and critical thinking.

items.title: Determinants of Mechanical Ventilator Adoption in Healthcare Emergency Settings
items.abstract: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is the recommended standard of care in many emergencies, yet its adoption by nursing professionals remains inconsistent. This research examines whether perceived clinical expertise is associated with emergency nurses' intention to use MV, directly and indirectly through trust in MV technology and attitude toward MV, and whether emergency severity moderates these associations. Emergency nurses (N = 236) were randomly assigned to one of four vignettes of decreasing acuity: cardiorespiratory arrest, severe hypoxaemia, chest trauma with respiratory compromise, and acute pulmonary oedema. Structural equation modelling showed that expertise was associated with trust and intention, trust with attitude, and attitude with intention; the serial indirect effect of expertise on intention through trust and attitude was significant. Because these constructs were measured concurrently, this effect is interpreted as an indirect association rather than as evidence of causal transmission. Higher severity strengthened the direct association between expertise and intention and weakened the association between trust and attitude, so that the serial indirect association declined as acuity increased. These findings are consistent with a shift from deliberative to automatic processing under time pressure and suggest that training should build expertise to automaticity for maximum-acuity scenarios while fostering trust in lower-acuity ones.

items.title: DEVELOPING MODERN PEDAGOGICAL COMPETENCIES OF ENGLISH TEACHERS IN DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS
items.abstract: This research paper investigates the structural components and practical mechanisms for enhancing the modern pedagogical competencies of English language educators operating within a digital learning environment. Through empirical analysis and methodological modeling, the integration of artificial intelligence, interactive platforms, and digital educational tools into foreign language instruction is thoroughly evaluated. Special attention is given to the practical application of the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework across secondary school grade levels, specifically focusing on vocabulary retention via spaced repetition systems and oral proficiency enhancement using audiovisual tools. Furthermore, the paper outlines critical strategies for fostering teacher adaptation, digital literacy, and information security in hybrid educational settings. The research outcomes offer actionable insights for secondary and higher education professionals seeking to align language pedagogy with the technological demands of the 21st century.

items.title: DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL COMPETENCIES OF THE 21ST-CENTURY LANGUAGE TEACHER IN A DIGITAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENT
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies is reshaping language education and redefining the professional role of the teacher. A contemporary language teacher is expected to combine subject knowledge, pedagogical expertise, intercultural communication skills, and the ability to select, evaluate, and use digital tools responsibly. This article examines the professional and technological competencies required by language teachers working in digital learning environments. It draws on a conceptual review of international frameworks and relevant educational literature, particularly UNESCO’s ICT Competency Framework for Teachers and the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu). The discussion identifies key competence areas: professional engagement, digital resource management, technology-enhanced teaching, assessment, learner empowerment, digital safety, and continuous professional development. It also considers opportunities offered by learning management systems, online communication platforms, digital assessment tools, and artificial intelligence. The analysis suggests that technology improves language learning only when it is connected to clear pedagogical objectives and inclusive teaching practices. Barriers such as unequal access, limited training, privacy risks, and excessive dependence on automated tools must also be addressed. The article concludes that effective teacher development requires sustained institutional support, reflective practice, and a balanced integration of technology with human interaction.

items.title: Digital Health Innovations and Well-Being of the Aged Population: A Theoretical Approach
items.abstract: Digital health innovations are increasingly reshaping the delivery of healthcare and creating new possibilities for supporting the well-being of ageing populations. From telemedicine and remote patient monitoring to mobile health applications, wearable devices, and artificial intelligence-enabled services, these technologies can improve access to healthcare, strengthen disease management, and promote greater independence among older adults. However, their implications for the well-being of the aged population extend beyond clinical outcomes and involve psychological, social, behavioral, and functional dimensions of ageing. The paper adopted a secondary source of data. This theoretical study examines the relationship between digital health innovations and the well-being of older adults by synthesizing insights from existing conceptual and empirical literature and adopted successful aging theory as a framework to the study. The study conceptualizes digital health as an enabling mechanism through which older adults can participate more actively in managing their health and maintaining social connectedness. In conclusion, disparities in digital access, privacy concerns, technological complexity, and age-related are key to the health benefits of the aging population. The study recommends a conceptual perspective that integrates technological, individual, and social factors to explain how digital health innovations can contribute to healthier, more autonomous, and socially connected ageing. items.title: Digital innovation and public acceptance of nuclear energy in the green transition
items.abstract: Public acceptance is widely regarded as a binding constraint on the contribution of nuclear energy to the green transition, yet claims that digital innovation will ease this constraint have rarely been examined against social science evidence. This topical review asks under what conditions digital innovation in nuclear energy systems, in particular digital twins, artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive maintenance and the digitally supported design, manufacture and operation of small modular reactors (SMRs), can contribute to public acceptance of nuclear energy. The analysis draws on five strands of scholarship that are seldom brought into contact with the technical literature: risk perception research, cultural theory of risk, the deficit and engagement models of science communication, the social licence to operate, and socio-technical transitions theory, which serves as the integrating framework. Reading techno-optimistic claims through these lenses, the review identifies three structural barriers: a cybersecurity paradox, whereby the connectivity that enables digital safety functions simultaneously expands the attack surface; an economic gap, specific to SMRs, whereby projected cost reductions rest on serial-production assumptions that recent project experience has not supported; and a transparency fallacy, whereby information disclosure is expected to build trust although meta-analytic evidence links the benefit and risk perceptions associated with acceptance to trust rather than to knowledge. These barriers are argued to interact: cyber incidents could act as trust-destroying signal events, cost failures could undermine perceived institutional competence, and one-way transparency tools leave procedural justice concerns unaddressed. The review concludes that digital innovation is more likely to support acceptance when it is embedded in genuinely participatory engagement, when institutions demonstrably manage the new risks digitalisation creates, when economic claims are validated rather than promised, and when regulatory frameworks confer procedural legitimacy. Absent these conditions, digitalisation risks reproducing deficit-model assumptions that acceptance research has long found wanting.

items.title: Digital Policing and Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Community Trust and Police Legitimacy in Abia State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examines the implications of digital policing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption in the Nigeria Police Force for community trust and police legitimacy, with particular reference to Abia State. Anchored in Procedural Justice Theory, the study adopts a qualitative desk-review design, synthesizing peer-reviewed literature on digital policing, algorithmic decision-making, and Nigerian police-community relations. Abia State, with a 2006 census population of 2,845,380 spread across seventeen local government areas, provides a densely populated, predominantly urban and semi-urban context in which the legitimacy consequences of digital policing carry direct relevance for millions of residents. The review finds that digital tools carry real potential to strengthen policing capacity, but that their value for legitimacy depends less on technical sophistication than on whether their deployment is experienced by citizens as fair, transparent, and respectful. Evidence from Nigerian policing scholarship indicates that public confidence in the police remains persistently low, human discretion continues to compromise the neutrality of ostensibly objective digital systems, and police-public digital interaction in Nigeria remains predominantly one-directional rather than participatory. The study argues that without deliberate attention to voice, neutrality, and trustworthiness, the introduction of AI and digital infrastructure into Nigerian policing risks reproducing, rather than resolving, the legitimacy deficits that have long characterized police-community relations, and recommends that digital policing reform in Abia State be paired with institutional accountability and genuine community engagement. items.title: Digital Readiness and Narrative Driven Competency of Teachers in Adopting Artificial Intelligence Enabled Classroom Teaching Strategies
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence enabled classroom‑teaching tools can rapidly generate narrative‑style learning resources, explanatory paragraphs, casestudy materials, and formative assessment prompts for learners [1]. However, effective classroom integration requires teachers to possess not only general digital readiness but also narrative competency: the capacity to evaluate AI‑produced narratives, correct factual inconsistencies, align AI‑generated content with curriculum standards, and deliver coherent lesson narratives suited for Filipino learners [2]. This quantitative survey‑based study examined the relationship between teachers’ digital readiness, narrative‑focused AI competency, and adoption of AI‑enabled classroom teaching strategies among 385 public‑ and private‑school teachers from Metro Manila and CALABARZON [3]. Anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), DigCompEdu Framework, and Diffusion of Innovation Theory [4, 5, 6], the survey instrument measured four independent variables: technical digital readiness, pedagogical‑narrative competency, ethical‑content‑validation competency, and professional‑development readiness [7]. Cronbach’s Alpha reliability testing recorded α = 0.914 for digital readiness and α = 0.899 for narrative‑AI competency [8]. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were computed using SPSS 26 [9]. Findings revealed that pedagogical‑narrative competency recorded the highest mean score (M = 3.78, SD = 0.70), while ethical‑content‑validation competency registered the lowest mean (M = 2.92, SD = 0.84) [10]. A strong positive correlation (r = 0.744, p < 0.001) existed between overall digital readiness narrative competency scores and AI‑enabled teaching‑strategy adoption [10]. Regression analysis confirmed that pedagogical‑narrative competency (β = 0.425, p < 0.001) was the strongest predictor of AI‑strategy adoption [10]. Limitations included purposive sampling, cross‑sectional design, self‑reported competency bias, and geographic scope limited to Metro Manila‑CALABARZON [11]. The study concluded that teachers must combine digital readiness with narrative‑content‑validation competency to deploy AI‑generated classroom materials responsibly [12]. Recommendations included DepEd‑aligned narrative‑AI pedagogy training, school‑based AI‑content‑ethics workshops, and localized guidelines for verifying AI‑generated narrative learning resources [13].

items.title: Digital Twins for indoor environmental quality optimisation: Insights from two case studies
items.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology links physical and virtual building environments, offering opportunities to improve indoor environmental quality (IEQ). This paper synthesises insights from two applied DT case studies: an educational classroom with occupancy and environmental sensing, and a residential living lab for data-driven lighting optimisation. BIM-based models were coupled with measured data to support DT analysis at the Digital Shadow level. Results show that integrating BIM with IoT data improves situational awareness, while purpose-driven geometric simplification enhances simulation efficiency and agreement with measurements. Persistent challenges include interoperability gaps, limited analytics in visualisation platforms, and communication constraints. The study highlights lighting as a practical entry point for scalable IEQ-oriented DT deployment.

items.title: Digitalisation de la fonction RH, cognition, bien-être au travail et performance organisationnelle: revue systématique multi-bases et cadre intégrateur à double voie
items.abstract: Objectif : expliquer pourquoi la digitalisation des ressources humaines (RH) est associée à des bénéfices organisationnels et à des contraintes psychosociales parfois simultanées. La fragmentation des synthèses sur l’e-HRM, le technostress et la gestion algorithmique justifie une analyse intégrée des mécanismes d’appropriation. Méthode : revue systématique à visée intégrative de publications de 2007 à 2026, recherches clôturées le 8 septembre 2026 dans Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Business Source Complete et PsycINFO. Cinquante-deux contributions ont atteint l’étape d’éligibilité , 39 ont été retenues et 13 exclues. La synthèse est narrative, structurée par mécanismes, aucun protocole n’a été préenregistré. Résultats : 27 publications datent de 2022 à 2026, l’audit descriptif initial distingue 24 études de crédibilité élevée et 15 de crédibilité modérée. La voie des ressources associe qualité, utilité, appropriation et autonomie. La voie des demandes associe complexité, surveillance, charge cognitive et technostress. Six travaux sur les technologies numériques générales servent d’appui conceptuel à cette seconde voie, sans valoir preuve directe en contexte RH. Contribution : un cadre à double voie distingue les résultats individuels observés du lien inter-niveaux entre bien-être et performance, proposé à la validation empirique. Mots-clés : digitalisation RH ; e-HRM ; appropriation ; Job Demands-Resources ; technostress ; algorithmic HRM ; revue systématique. Type d’article : revue systématique intégrative. Classification JEL : M12 ; M54 ; O33. Abstract Objective: to explain why digital human resource management (HRM) is associated with organizational benefits as well as psychosocial constraints. Fragmented reviews of e-HRM, technostress and algorithmic management call for an integrated account of appropriation mechanisms. Methods: an integrative systematic review of publications from 2007 to 2026, with searches closed on 8 September 2026 in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Business Source Complete and PsycINFO. Fifty-two contributions reached eligibility assessment; 39 were included and 13 excluded. A mechanism-oriented narrative synthesis was used; no protocol was preregistered. Results: 27 publications appeared in 2022-2026; the initial descriptive appraisal classified 24 studies as higher credibility and 15 as moderate credibility. The resource pathway links system quality, perceived usefulness, appropriation and autonomy. The demand pathway involves complexity, monitoring, cognitive load and technostress. Six studies on general workplace technologies inform the demand pathway conceptually, rather than providing direct evidence for HR-specific systems. Contribution: the dual-path framework separates documented individual outcomes from the proposed, still untested, multilevel relationship between employee well-being and organizational performance. Keywords: digital HRM; e-HRM; technology appropriation; Job Demands-Resources; technostress; algorithmic HRM; systematic review. Article type: integrative systematic review. items.title: Direct wireless large language model inference from high-altitude platform stations under payload constraints
items.abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPS) could extend 6G non-terrestrial networks from wireless access to onboard AI inference, but serving capacity is jointly constrained by computing, thermal management , radio circuitry and finite payload resources. We develop a cross-layer framework combining a 110-day LLM workload trace, concurrency-dependent latency, stochastic user activity, thermal simulation , radio-power modelling and reported HAPS payload limits. Long-context requests account for only 1.35% of elapsed-time occupancy yet consume 48.6% of the serving budget for the evaluated 70B configuration. Under a 5% model-defined compute-overload criterion, the 8B/1×H100 and 70B/2×H100 configurations support 5,876 and 991 user equivalents. Integrating computing, thermal, communication, power and mass constraints yields platform-level capacities up to 7,245 and 23,144 user equivalents for Sunglider-class and Stratobus-class platforms. These results show that long-context demand, heat-rejection capability and payload power—not accelerator throughput alone—govern HAPS-based LLM inference feasibility in 6G NTN.

items.title: Displacement of Discriminating Questions by Expected Response Costs: Why Some Questions Are Easier to Ask
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Displacement of Discriminating Questions by Expected Response Costs, a mechanism by which the anticipated consequences of obtaining an answer shift inquiry away from a question that would materially distinguish the alternatives relevant to a decision. A different question may be easier to pursue, less disruptive, or less likely to create an obligation to act. The inquiry continues, but the evidential distinction most important to the decision can remain unresolved. The paper assesses the mechanism by identifying the discriminating question, establishing whether it was recognized and could have been pursued, and examining what consequences its answer was expected to bring. These may include delay, strained relationships, additional responsibilities, or reconsideration of an existing commitment. A substitute question need not be irrelevant or improperly chosen. Cost sensitivity can be justified, and omission alone does not establish avoidance. The mechanism requires evidence that the expected response cost influenced which question was selected while the evidential need remained. The first documented case concerns the Metropolitan Museum of Art's 1972 acquisition of the Euphronios krater for one million dollars. Trustee Arthur Ochs Sulzberger asked whether the ancient vase had been tested, and director Thomas Hoving promised laboratory examination. Hoving later recalled harboring doubts about documents supporting the vase's provenance but withholding those doubts from the acquisitions committee. The second case concerns an investment venture involving Viktor Kozeny and Azerbaijani oil privatization. During a recorded conference call on May 18, 1999, investor Frederic Bourke asked what a person should do upon being told that an official had received a payment. The appellate record also describes another investment firm's investigation and decision not to participate. Both cases document parts of the proposed mechanism without establishing that anticipated costs caused the selection of a substitute question. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the paper places the mechanism alongside research on deliberate ignorance and examines how anticipated consequences influence the direction of inquiry. A prospective human–AI application concerns an evaluation assistant that checks whether a model's output satisfies formatting requirements while avoiding a harder question about the reliability of its sources because an unfavorable answer would require delaying deployment. Establishing the mechanism would require evidence that the harder question was recognized, feasible, and displaced because of its expected consequences.

items.title: Do Digital Nudges Survive Complexity? Cognitive Biases and AI Assistance in Time-Series Financial Decisions
items.abstract: Most evidence for digital nudges comes from simple choice sets. We test whether they still work in information-dense financial interfaces and how AI assistants affect them. In an online experiment, 252 participants from Armenia managed a two-currency portfolio and made buy, hold, or sell decisions on dynamic time-series charts. Each participant saw five of ten manipulations under one of four AI conditions: no assistant or a neutral, biased, or debiasing assistant. Four manipulations shifted choices toward their target actions. A stated 70% chance of growth had the largest effect (+36.5 percentage points), followed by adding a third, decoy forecast to the two-forecast control set (+29.4 pp relative to that set), an upward price spike (+25.4 pp), and red highlighting of losses (+23.8 pp). The rest, including social proof and anchoring, had no significant effect. Paired nudges worked differently by direction: numeric and verbal cues mainly pushed buying, and the red cue pushed selling. A biased assistant roughly doubled the odds of the target action, while neutral and debiasing assistants had no detectable effect. Specific cues in the price chart still work in complex displays, and AI strengthens them more easily than it corrects them.

items.title: Don't Take the Researcher Out of Research: Perspectives on AI from Qualitative Scholars
items.abstract: In line with the explosion of public, political, and educational discourses around the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) in everyday life, researchers have recently invested a significant amount of time into exploring and theorizing the use of AI in qualitative data analysis. This proposed use of AI creates a theoretical friction with qualitative methodologists who foreground the interpretive (and essentially human) elements of this research praxis. To productively engage with this friction, authors--who span from being more quantitatively oriented to those who are considered Big Q Qualitative researchers--engaged in conversations with one another in a reflexive process of self-study. To help facilitate these conversations, all the authors explored CAILA, a qualitative analysis tool that uses AI to autonomously generate codes and themes from a text-based data set. Authors familiar with the tool spoke to the other three scholars who begrudgingly experimented with CAILA for the first--and last--time. Analysis of these conversations showed that participants felt that AI-based research tools could support menial aspects of qualitative analysis or help with coding of data based on established codebooks. However, the participants also found that tools like CAILA failed to provide meaningful interpretations of the data and stripped the humanistic components of qualitative research from the analysis process. These findings sit in opposition to the purported value of AI software, which emphasizes the efficiency of research processes. To this end, our findings position qualitative research as a human pursuit, asserting that the slow pace of the coding processes provides the space needed for researchers to develop new ideas and meaning from bodies of text. We contribute to the ongoing conversation about using AI for qualitative data analysis by providing fresh perspectives from Big Q Qualitative methodologists and inviting the field to think more deeply about the qualitative research process.

items.title: Dual Active Learning for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
items.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is critical to recent advances in generative artificial intelligence. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely applied to achieve this objective. A key step in RLHF is to learn the reward function from human feedback. However, human feedback is costly and time-consuming, making it essential to collect high-quality conversation data for human teachers to label. Additionally, different human teachers have different levels of expertise. It is thus critical to query the most appropriate teacher for their opinions. In this paper, we use offline reinforcement learning (RL) to formulate the alignment problem. Motivated by the idea of $D$-optimal design, we first propose a dual active reward learning algorithm for the simultaneous selection of conversations and teachers. Next, we apply pessimistic RL to solve the alignment problem, based on the learned reward estimator. Theoretically, we show that the reward estimator obtained through our proposed adaptive selection strategy achieves minimal generalized variance asymptotically, and prove that the sub-optimality of our pessimistic policy scales as $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ with a given sample budget $T$. Through simulations and experiments on LLMs, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm and its superiority over state-of-the-art.

items.title: Dual evaluation mechanism of artificial intelligence enabled fintech discontinuance for sustainable financial inclusion in India
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now underpins FinTech services that support digital financial inclusion and sustainable economic growth, yet AI-enabled fraud threatens users' trust in this innovation. Some users intend to discontinue AI-enabled FinTech services even when they are satisfied and habituated, a pattern that traditional continuance explanations do not explain. This study examines a Dual Evaluation Mechanism in which discontinuance intention forms through an internal path (confirmation, satisfaction, and habit) and an external path (vicarious exposure to AI fraud and perceived AI fraud risk), and tests whether perceived AI fraud risk moderates the relationship between habit and discontinuance intention. The study employs cross-sectional survey data from 507 Indian users of AI-enabled FinTech services, analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling and complemented by predictive, importance-performance, endogeneity, and necessary condition analyses. The results show that confirmation raises satisfaction (β = 0.648), satisfaction raises habit (β = 0.578), and habit lowers discontinuance intention (β = −0.330). Vicarious AI fraud exposure raises perceived AI fraud risk (β = 0.588), which raises discontinuance intention (β = 0.507), and the interaction between risk and habit is positive (β = 0.174); all paths are significant at p < 0.001. The model explains 39.9% of the variance in discontinuance intention and outperforms the indicator-average benchmark in out-of-sample prediction. The findings suggest that all six hypotheses are supported, that perceived AI fraud risk is the most important predictor of discontinuance intention (0.507) and weakens the protective effect of habit, and that no construct is a strong necessary condition for discontinuance (d ≤ 0.163). items.title: E-Grampanchayat: AI-Powered Smart Village Administration System
items.abstract: Gram Panchayats are the first point of contact between rural citizens and the government, yet many of their services, such as certificates, tax collection and complaint handling, still depend on paper registers, repeated visits to the panchayat office and the availability of a single village official. This paper presents the design of E-Grampanchayat, an AI-powered smart village administration system built with Python. The system provides a multilingual citizen portal for certificate applications, house and water tax payment, grievance registration and scheme information, together with an administrative dashboard for the Sarpanch and the Gram Sevak. Lightweight artificial intelligence components based on natural language processing (NLTK/spaCy) and machine learning (scikit-learn) classify citizen requests, assign grievances a category and priority, route them to the responsible official, and answer common questions through a chatbot in Marathi, Hindi and English. The system is organised as a linear five-stage pipeline that is easy to understand, extend and run on modest hardware. The paper describes the architecture, technology stack, request-processing flow, applications, advantages and limitations, a privacy and security analysis and a planned evaluation, and outlines future work including voice interaction, DigiLocker integration, IoT-based village services and predictive analytics.

items.title: EFFECTIVE WAYS TO USE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TEACHING ENGLISH AS A FOREIGN LANGUAGE (EFL)
items.abstract: This thesis examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used effectively in teaching English as a foreign language. It reviews the theoretical grounds for AI-supported instruction and describes five pedagogically sound applications: automated writing feedback, conversational practice with chatbots and voice assistants, adaptive personalization, generative AI for materials development, and AI-assisted assessment. It also considers risks such as over-reliance, accuracy problems, and ethical concerns. The analysis suggests that AI is most effective when it complements, rather than replaces, the teacher, when it is tied to clear learning objectives, and when learners are trained to use it critically.

items.title: Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence Interventions in Higher Education: A PRISMA 2020 Systematic Review with Structured Narrative Synthesis
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being adopted in university teaching faster than evidence on its instructional value is being consolidated. This systematic review examined whether AI-based interventions improve achievement, engagement, satisfaction, and knowledge retention among undergraduate and graduate students relative to conventional instruction. Following PRISMA 2020, seven queries in SciSpace, Google Scholar, and PubMed, run on September 23, 2026, identified 902 records. After deduplication and a relevance-ranking cut-off, 500 records were screened, 82 reports were assessed for eligibility, and the 80 provisionally eligible reports were verified against publisher, index, or repository records. Reports that could not be verified (n = 52), proved ineligible (n = 4), or existed only as non-peer-reviewed preprints (n = 2) were excluded, leaving 22 peer-reviewed reports: 14 primary comparative studies and eight meta-analyses. Evidence was integrated through a structured narrative synthesis without meta-analysis, using design-based robustness indicators. Five primary studies were randomised. Meta-analyses restricted to higher-education students reported moderate effects on achievement in college populations (Hedges’ g = 0.32–0.53) and inconsistent effects in medical education (SMD = 0.27–2.06); broader-population syntheses were treated as contextual only. Primary studies were favourable when AI was embedded in structured pedagogical designs, whereas comparisons with well-designed conventional or human instruction often showed no advantage, and unguided generative AI use improved immediate performance more than retention or transfer. Given the small, largely non-randomised evidence base and declared departures from standard search practice, the evidence supports only tentative, design-dependent claims about AI in higher education.

items.title: Effects of Blended AI-Assisted and Teacher-Led Instruction on EFL Students’ Academic Writing Development and Writing Self-Efficacy at Salale University, Ethiopia
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has entered Ethiopian higher education faster than pedagogical frameworks for its use. This study examined the effects of a blended model combining AI-assisted feedback with teacher-led instruction on EFL students’ academic writing development and writing self-efficacy. A one-group pre-test–post-test quasi-experimental design with an embedded qualitative strand was used. Thirty-seven third-year students of the Department of English Language and Literature at Salale University, enrolled in the Intermediate Writing course, received ten weeks of blended instruction in which AI tools supplied immediate draft-level feedback and the teacher supplied genre, content and revision instruction. Teaching materials were modified from the existing course textbook rather than newly prepared. Writing was assessed with an adapted analytic rubric and self-efficacy with the Second Language Writer Self-Efficacy Scale. Paired-samples t-tests showed significant gains in overall writing, from M = 51.38 to M = 64.22, t (36) = 10.00, p < .001, d = 1.64, and in writing self-efficacy, from M = 2.84 to M = 3.73, t (36) = 9.33, p < .001, d = 1.53. Gains were largest for content and organization and smallest for mechanics. Writing and self-efficacy gains correlated moderately, r = .46, p = .004.

items.title: Efficiency Without Quality? A Six Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) Field Study of Sub-Intent Library Curation in a Live Airline Chatbot
items.abstract: This study asks whether the Six Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) cycle can improve utterance capture in a live enterprise chatbot, and how much of the change is attributable to the intervention during a concurrent migration to large language model (LLM) components. Turkish WhatsApp utterances of Turkish Airlines’ TK Assistant (80,295 utterances, January–July 2025) was analyzed; utterance capture scores (success threshold 0.95) were graded on a five-level scale, with 0.95 as the success threshold. After bidirectional Pareto analysis, 349 Strong-band utterances without a verbatim counterpart were added to ten sub-intent libraries. Assessment used utterance-level re-capture analysis against non-added controls, expected-versus-actual attribution, Laney p′ charts and blind human validation of 300 utterances. Recurring added texts were captured as exact matches (17 of 22 at first recurrence, against none of eight recurring controls; difference 77 points, 95% confidence interval 39–90), without organic promotion beyond near-identical forms. Under stated assumptions, the intervention was followed by 69 additional exact matches, while the successful utterance capture rate fell from 21.04% to 16.11%, a decline inseparable from the migration. Annotators judged exact matches correctly routed no more often than Strong-band matches (87% vs. 98%, p = 0.032 jointly, marginal per annotator). Verbatim curation buys exact-match efficiency, not understanding; confidence-based metrics should be secondary improvement targets.

items.title: Emotion-associated representations in the feed forward gates of a language model
items.abstract: Identifying emotion-associated neurons in large language models does not establish how those neurons contribute to emotional behavior. This study investigates that distinction through three levels of explanation: representation, reconfiguration, and causal control. Statistically corrected feed-forward activation signatures in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct exhibited structured overlap corresponding to a psychological circumplex model, with substantial but incomplete reproducibility across Chinese texts and their English translations. Four experimental task families investigated whether these signatures changed with behavioral demands and predicted model outputs. The preregistered internal measure failed held-out validation, with only two of fourteen hypotheses supported; post hoc corrected measures revealed task-dependent reconfiguration and several associations with behavioral measures. However, increased internal separation did not consistently improve discrimination accuracy, evidence-specific changes depended on the internal measure, and static neuronal overlap did not predict generated-text confusability under the designated classifier, although a secondary lexicon analysis showed the predicted association. Suppression of emotional expression was not accompanied by a reliably detected change at the sampled pre-generation position. These findings demonstrate that emotion-associated activation structure and task responsiveness do not, by themselves, provide a general explanation of emotional behavior. The study establishes the need to distinguish representational association, task-dependent reconfiguration, and causal control, the last of which remains untested.

items.title: Emotional Superintelligence: A New Paradigm for Compassionate Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has achieved significant advances in perception, language generation, reasoning, and decision-making. However, current Artificial Intelligence systems primarily optimize task performance and remain limited in their ability to account for emotional context, ethical considerations, and long-term human well-being. Existing research on Emotional Intelligence, Affective Computing, Compassionate Artificial Intelligence and Theory of Mind addresses different aspects of this challenge, but these capabilities have largely been studied independently. We propose Emotional Superintelligence as a new computational paradigm that integrates contextual emotional understanding, compassion, ethical reasoning, human-value alignment, and well-being-oriented decision-making into a unified Artificial Intelligence framework and introduce a five-layer model. Our Model adopts a functional view of emotional understanding, focusing not on whether an Artificial Intelligence system subjectively experiences emotions, but on how effectively it interprets emotional context and uses that information to make responsible and compassionate decisions. Potential implementation pathways for Large Language Models and autonomous systems are recommended along with applications in diversified domains such as healthcare, education, governance, and Human-Artificial Intelligence interaction. We also identify key challenges concerning multi-modal emotion understanding, emotional bias, manipulation, privacy, human oversight, and long-term well-being. By integrating emotional and ethical capabilities into the Artificial Intelligence decision process, Emotional Superintelligence reframes intelligent-system development from task optimization alone towards responsible human flourishing and provides a research agenda for future compassionate and socially beneficial Artificial Intelligence.

items.title: End-to-end AI-assisted generation of HAZOP study reports in the process industries
items.abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end AI-assisted framework for the automated generation of hazard and operability (HAZOP) reports to address key challenges of current HAZOP practices, including time consumption, human bias, and knowledge loss. The framework consists of four modules, each employing a set of artificial intelligence (AI) models to support the generation of HAZOP notes, including deviations, causes, consequences, safeguards, and recommendations. The First module assesses the degree of similarity (expressed in 3 levels: high, medium, or low) between current and past piping and instrumentation diagram (P&ID) nodes using object, location, and functional similarity metrics. Object and location similarities are computed using the detected classes and bounding boxes coordinates obtained from YOLO models, while functional similarity is derived from node descriptions generated by large language models (LLMs). These metrics are then combined to compute the P&ID Node Similarity Index (PNSI), which determines the similarity level to guide subsequent analysis. For the high level, the associated HAZOP notes are directly retrieved and reused. For the medium level, the second module employs BERTopic to identify dominant topics from retrieved HAZOP notes. items.title: Enhancing Intangible Cultural Heritage Dance Formation Choreography in VR via Large Language Models
items.abstract: The recent popularity of consumer-grade virtual reality devices has enabled users to experience immersive Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) dances in virtual environments, where ICH is defined by UNESCO as traditions or living expressions inherited from our ancestors. As in real-world choreography, the dancers in a virtual environment should be instructed in how to perform their dance. However, this can be a time-consuming and challenging task with the current Virtual Reality (VR) controllers. To address these challenges, we introduce an innovative choreography system leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate dance creation and presentation in VR. To achieve this goal, we first establish a corpus dataset comprising almost 5,000 prompt phrases to describe fundamental movements and formation changes within dance formation choreography. We then leverage an LLM to understand these prompts, thereby comprehending the commands issued by users during the interaction. Based on the understanding provided by the LLM, these prompts are converted into primitive commands that our system can execute. This allows the virtual character to perform corresponding actions to complete the dance formation choreography. We conduct three user studies with 94 subjects to validate the proposed approach. Through user studies, we find that the proposed approach can help users generate high-quality ICH dances regarding human likeness, appropriateness, and operability. items.title: Entropy-Adaptive Hybrid Artificial Intelligence with Dynamic Weighted Fu-sion for Intrusion Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks
items.abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely used in safety-critical cyber-physical environments, including smart grids, industrial automation, healthcare monitoring, disaster management, and defence surveillance. However, their distributed operation, limited computational resources, and exposure to diverse traffic patterns make them highly susceptible to sophisticated cyberattacks. Existing intrusion detection approaches often employ static ensemble strategies with fixed classifier weights, which can reduce detection effectiveness when network conditions and attack characteristics change dynamically. This study proposes an entropy-adaptive Hybrid Artificial Intelligence with Dynamic Weighted Fusion (HAI-DWF) framework for real-time intrusion detection and attack classification in WSNs. The proposed architecture combines a convolutional neural network for spatial feature extraction, a bidi-rectional long short-term memory network with temporal self-attention for sequential traffic modelling, and LightGBM for efficient learning from structured network features. A dynamic weighted fusion mechanism is in-troduced to adapt classifier contributions according to Shannon entropy computed from incoming traffic, allowing the detection process to respond to variations in attack behaviour and traffic uncertainty. Because the contribution of the entropy signal itself has to be demonstrated rather than assumed, validation protocols for entropy ablation against learned-gate, stacking and alternative-entropy fusion, multi-seed repetition, leakage-free cross-dataset transfer, problem-space adversarial feasibility and end-to-end embedded measurement are specified in Sections 3.9–3.12. The framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets, namely CICIoT-2023, Edge-IIoTset-2022, NF-ToN-IoT-v2, and WSN-DS. Experimental results show that HAI-DWF achieves 99.46% accuracy, a 99.27% F1-score, and a false positive rate of 0.31% on CICIoT-2023, while maintaining strong performance across the remaining datasets. Edge-oriented profiling on ARM Cortex-M55 and RISC-V SiFive U74 platforms indicates the inference-level computational feasibility of the proposed framework on cluster-head-class devices, with end-to-end measurements of feature extraction, communication, memory and energy specified in Section 3.12. Robustness analysis under FGSM, PGD, DeepFool, and C&W adversarial attacks shows a much smaller accuracy loss than the neural components alone, which is attributable mainly to the LightGBM component; these feature-space results are complemented by a problem-space feasibility protocol (Section 3.11). These results indicate that HAI-DWF is a promising adaptive and deployment-oriented intrusion detection approach, whose entropy-specific contribution remains subject to the validation experiments specified in this revision for WSN- and IoT-enabled cyber-physical systems.

items.title: Epistemic blind spots in protein function prediction: uncertainty, homology bias and failure modes in deep learning models
items.abstract: Protein function prediction has advanced from homology-based annotation transfer to deep learning, protein language models, and multimodal foundation models. Yet improved benchmark performance does not resolve a more basic problem: these systems learn from biological knowledge that is incomplete, heterogeneous in evidential support, and strongly structured by evolutionary relationships. We organize this problem as two sequentially dependent epistemological levels. The first concerns biological knowledge: what functional states become observable, with what evidential support and evolutionary structure. The second concerns what models can legitimately infer from that supervision, including representation sufficiency, uncertainty, generalization, and the scope of a universal computational blueprint for protein function inference. Because limitations at the first level enter the learning problem before model fitting, benchmark performance and model uncertainty cannot by themselves establish certainty about latent biological function. Trustworthy protein AI therefore requires explicit attention to applicability domains, distribution shift, uncertainty, and the limits of inference from available biological knowledge.

items.abstract: This article examines the design and validation of a leadership-mediated internal communication strategy aimed at strengthening the organizational culture of Outsourcing S.A.S. BIC. The study adopted a qualitative approach, incorporating descriptive elements and an exploratory and propositional scope. The diagnostic phase included document analysis, the Organizational Culture Assessment Instrument (OCAI), audience surveys, and focus groups. Two iterative prototyping cycles followed in Outsourcing S.A.S. BIC’s UARIV telephone account: a problem prototype validated with seven middle managers and a solution prototype implemented with 78 employees working remotely fromdifferent locations across Colombia. At the interim assessment, conducted six weeks after the strategy was launched, improvements in shift adherence (from 60.05% to 96.09%) and productivity (from 53.08% to 93.16%) coincided with the prototype activation period, although the research design does not establish a causal relationship. Findings highlight the relevance of leadership- driven cultural mediation supported by narratives, rituals, microformats, and continuous listening. Artificial intelligence proved useful as an analytical and support tool without replacing human interaction.

items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the relationship between job stress and job performance among clinical healthcare personnel in two public healthcare contexts in Peru and Brazil. ​Methodology: A quantitative, observational, cross-sectional, and comparative-correlational design was implemented. The sample comprised 60 healthcare professionals (30 from Hospital Jesús Nazareno, Ayacucho, Peru, and 30 from Universidad Nacional Ecológica, representing Brazil). Data were gathered using the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI-HSS) and the Individual Work Performance Questionnaire (IWPQ). Descriptive statistics, Spearman’s Rho coefficient, and the Mann-Whitney U test were applied. Results: In the overall sample (N = 60), total stress correlated positively with performance (ρ = 0.3475; p = 0.0065), with depersonalization showing the strongest association (ρ = 0.4956). When analyzed separately by facility, intra-hospital correlations lost statistical significance (ρ = 0.1741 in Brazil; ρ = -0.1697 in Peru). The Mann-Whitney U test showed significantly higher scores in Brazil for total stress (81.93 vs. 59.67; U = 132.0) and job performance (61.50 vs. 48.00; U = 176.5). ​Conclusions: Depersonalization functions as an adaptive defense mechanism to sustain task execution under pressure. Inter-institutional disparities highlight the influence of management models on occupational health.

items.title: Ethical Guidelines for Judges and Prosecutors on the Responsible use of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The AI guidelines, developed within the EU’s EL PACCTO 2.0 programme, set an ethical framework for judges and prosecutors in Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean who use Artificial Intelligence. Their core principle is that AI may assist but must never decide, so every decision stays with a human who is fully accountable for it. Judges and prosecutors must verify every AI output, keep confidential and judicial data out of public chatbots, and use only systems with the highest cybersecurity standards. Institutions should publicly disclose which AI systems they use and favour secure, locally hosted tools that use resources sparingly. Ongoing training and binding codes of conduct should help them use AI critically and avoid automation bias. In criminal justice, the guidelines add stronger safeguards for the presumption of innocence, the rights of the defence and the right to challenge evidence produced with AI.

items.title: Evaluating Output Consistency and Potential Information Leakage in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for business planning and decision support, raising concerns about whether user-provided information may persist or reappear in later outputs. This exploratory study evaluated apparent information leakage and output persistence across ChatGPT, Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Microsoft Copilot. Twenty fictional business plans were entered into the models using free individual accounts; half included an explicit confidentiality instruction. For 14 days, extraction prompts were submitted in incognito sessions without logging into an account, alternating between two devices. Outputs were reviewed qualitatively for possible reproduction of original business-plan details and quantitatively using word counts and Jaccard similarity scores. Results showed significant differences in output length and similarity across models. Copilot produced the most lexically consistent outputs over time, while Gemini produced the least consistent outputs. Device condition had a statistically significant but small effect. items.title: Evaluating the Impact of Self-Reported RAG-AI Engagement on Academic Performance: A Longitudinal Study of NotebookLM in Medical Education
items.abstract: Introduction: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can minimise large language model hallucinations while supporting self-regulated learning. We evaluated the impact of student engagement with a grounded RAG-AI tool (Google NotebookLM) on formative and internal assessment scores in undergraduate pathology, validated a 3-item AI Disclosure Form, and explored cognitive adoption barriers. Methods In a 12-week longitudinal study using an interrupted time series design, Phase II medical students (N = 211) received curated NotebookLM modules alongside core lectures. Students completed weekly quizzes, a 3-item disclosure form assessing the frequency, application mode, and trust in the AI resources, and end-of-study mixed-method questionnaires. Longitudinal cohorts were classified into High, Low, Inconsistent, and non-usage groups, with differences evaluated via ANOVA. Results The 3-item disclosure form demonstrated high reliability. The average scores of formative quizzes (p = 0.656) and summative internal exams (p = 0.961) did not differ significantly between the engagement groups. However, there were notable differences in performance during some of the dense, complex sections (Lung, p < 0.001; Renal, p < 0.001). Frequent users used active Socratic chat and self-quizzing to handle high cognitive demands. In contrast, inconsistent users showed "cognitive flight" under stress, and non-respondents scored significantly lower (24.83 ± 13.76). Conclusion A standalone RAG-AI tool does not automatically improve the overall performance of a group. Instead, it helps manage cognitive load during demanding modules for learners who are good at self-regulated learning. Future use needs structured workflows within a Learning Management System and training for prompt verification.

items.title: Evaluating the Usability of an AI-Based Nutrition App Among Female Breast Cancer Survivors in Philadelphia, PA, USA: The CANEAT Pilot Focus Group Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Access to personalized nutrition counseling for cancer survivors is limited and often mirrors socioeconomic status. We hypothesized that the CANEAT application (app), a novel large language model (LLM)-based tool developed by our team, would provide usable, culturally relevant, and affordable dietary recommendations to support female breast cancer survivors treated with radiation therapy (RT) in managing long-term nutritional needs. Methods: In this single-institution pilot mixed-methods study at Thomas Jefferson University (Philadelphia, PA, USA), female breast cancer survivors with prior RT were enrolled from August 2025 to May 2026 to participate in focus groups to test the CANEAT AI app. Demographic information was collected and inputted into the LLM, which then generated personalized meal plans and grocery lists delivered through the app interface. The participants reviewed the plans and completed the validated System Usability Scale (SUS). Then a group discussion with structured questions was conducted, recorded, and transcribed. The primary endpoint was a SUS usability score > 70. Thematic analysis was applied to focus group transcripts using NVivo for qualitative themes. Results: Three focus groups were conducted consisting of 10 participants (50% were 65 years or older; 100% were female; 60% were racial/ethnic minorities; 100% with prior RT). The mean SUS score was 84.25 (SD 13.44; range 60.0–100.0), with 80% rating the app as acceptable (>70). Analysis of qualitative themes highlighted high cultural relevance, the ability to have grocery lists within budget constraints, and geographic feasibility. The main limitation participants identified was that the app did not address RT side effects. Agreement between the two qualitative coders was fair (κ = 0.34–0.35). Conclusions: In this small pilot study of female breast cancer survivors at a single institution in Philadelphia, CANEAT demonstrated high usability among a technologically experienced cohort. These preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings do not establish clinical benefit, safety, or an effect on nutritional disparities, and warrant validation in larger, multi-center domestic and international cohorts that include other cancer types, male patients, and participants with lower digital literacy, with a comparator arm, and long-term follow-up.

items.title: Examining HiTOP Through Naturalistic Symptom Descriptions in Anonymous Online Mental Health Forums: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
items.abstract: AbstractBackground: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) organises covarying symptoms and maladaptive traits into transdiagnostic dimensions to address limitations of categorical diagnosis. Naturalistic symptom descriptions may complement structured assessments. Objective: This protocol describes a reproducible mixed-methods workflow to derive symptom indicators from forum posts and examine their organisation relative to HiTOP. Methods and analysis: The target sample is 80,000 public Reddit posts. After local de-identification, a large language model (LLM) will extract symptom labels and supporting paraphrases. Two human experts will independently review outputs for up to 250 posts. Three embedding models will flag potentially equivalent symptom labels for local LLM assessment. Two experts will qualitatively review the most frequent canonical symptom labels (at least 1,000) and develop a codebook of symptom categories, continuing until a prespecified saturation criterion is met. An LLM will assign canonical symptom labels to these categories, producing binary post-level indicators. Multiverse-inspired structural analyses will compare network, component, factor, and clustering representations across discovery, internal tuning, and holdout partitions. Evaluation will assess interpretability, stability, and agreement with expert mapping to HiTOP. Supplementary analyses will include agent-assisted exploration, codebook application to DepressionEmo and the Reddit Mental Health Dataset, and pooled integrative analysis that may include additional comparable corpora.Discussion: The study will examine whether symptom co-expression within posts forms interpretable patterns corresponding to HiTOP.Ethics: The Ethics Committee of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin approved the study (EA2/274/25). The study was preregistered on 8 May 2026 (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00040244).Keywords: Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology, natural language processing, large language models, Reddit, mixed methods, study protocol

items.title: Explainable AI Based Blood Disorder Screening
items.abstract: Blood disorders such as anaemia, leukemia, thalassemia, and thrombocytopenia significantly affect human health and require early identification for effective treatment. Conventional diagnostic procedures often involve manual interpretation of blood test results, which may lead to delays and variations in clinical assessment. This research proposes an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based blood disorder screening system that integrates machine learning and deep learning techniques to improve screening accuracy and reliability. The system analyses haematological parameters, including haemoglobin, red blood cell count, white blood cell count, platelet count, and other complete blood count (CBC) features to identify potential abnormalities. Explainability techniques such as SHAP and LIME provide transparent interpretations of model predictions by highlighting influential parameters. The proposed system supports early screening, improves clinical decision-making, and assists healthcare professionals in delivering reliable diagnostic recommendations.

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Financial Decisions: The Role of Trust, Transparency, and Financial Literacy.
items.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into financial services has transformed how consumers access financial information, evaluate financial alternatives, and make financial decisions. Although AI-driven financial applications offer opportunities to improve decision efficiency, personalization, and accessibility, their adoption raises concerns regarding algorithmic opacity, perceived risk, and consumer trust. In this context, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as an important approach to improving the transparency and interpretability of AI-generated financial recommendations. This study examines how explainability and transparency shape consumer trust and influence financial decision-making, while considering financial literacy as a relevant individual-level factor. Drawing on behavioral economics, trust in automation theory, and information asymmetry perspectives, the study develops an integrative conceptual framework linking perceived AI explainability, algorithmic transparency, consumer trust, and financial decision outcomes. The analysis conceptualizes consumer trust as a key mechanism through which explainable AI may influence the acceptance and use of AI-generated financial recommendations. It further highlights financial literacy as a potential moderating factor that shapes consumers' ability to understand algorithmic explanations, assess financial risks, and critically evaluate AI-based advice. The study argues that explainability alone does not guarantee informed financial decisions, as its effectiveness also depends on consumers' financial knowledge, perceived reliability, and ability to interpret the information provided. By integrating technological explainability with psychological trust and financial literacy, this study contributes to the literature on digital finance and behavioral economics through a conceptual framework for understanding consumer responses to AI-mediated financial decision-making. The findings offer implications for financial institutions, AI developers, and policymakers in designing transparent, accountable, and consumer-centered AI-based financial services.

items.title: Explainable Multimodal AI for Early Cardiometabolic Risk Assessment Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Wearable Data: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic conditions, including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity and hypertension, develop through complex interactions among metabolic, physiological and lifestyle factors. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and wearable devices can capture time-resolved information such as glucose patterns, heart rate, physical activity and sleep. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have been investigated for glucose forecasting, physiological-state estimation, disease screening, prospective risk stratification and management of established conditions. This narrative review examines seventeen primary studies and one systematic review relevant to early cardiometabolic risk assessment, with particular attention to multimodal data integration, temporal modelling, explainable AI (XAI) and personalised preventive guidance. The reviewed primary studies cover digital-twin-based diabetes management, insulin resistance, glucose prediction, multi-task disease prediction, prediabetes screening, explainable obesity assessment, wearable-based blood-pressure assessment and CGM-based long-term risk stratification. GluFormer demonstrates prospective risk stratification from CGM representations and a dietary-data extension. The remaining gap is narrower: the included evidence does not establish one externally validated framework that jointly assesses multiple cardiometabolic conditions using CGM and broader wearable/clinical modalities while providing validated explanations and evaluated personalised preventive guidance. The review discusses validation, label quality, privacy and ethical challenges. Such systems should be evaluated using participant-level data separation, external validation and uncertainty assessment, and their outputs should be communicated as non-diagnostic risk estimates rather than clinical diagnoses.

items.title: Exploring AI-Supported Disciplinary Mediation in Student Project Teams' Text-Based Communication: A Probe-Grounded Co-Design Study
items.abstract: Interdisciplinary student teams must negotiate differences in terminology, priorities, and practices, yet these differences are difficult to surface in text-based communication. We introduce Spritz, a Discord-based LLM technology probe designed to create a situated experience of AI-mediated collaboration for reflection and co-design. Spritz detects semantic or pragmatic tensions, privately prompts members to articulate their perspectives, and returns anonymized syntheses to group discussion. We conducted an exploratory study and co-design workshop with 12 students from technical, business, and design backgrounds. Preliminary findings suggest that participants perceived AI mediation along cognitive and relational dimensions. Spritz helped organize fragmented discussions, surface implicit reasoning, and reduce interpersonal pressure around disagreement. Participants also envisioned AI as a strategic advisor, cross-domain translator, and perspective challenger, raising tensions around neutrality, authority, and accountability. We discuss implications for negotiable interventions, transparent role transitions, and preserving human ownership of team decisions.

items.title: Exploring Discrete Algorithms in Quantum Computing
items.abstract: Quantum computing introduces a new computational paradigm by extending the classical binary representation of information through quantum bits, which can exist in superposed states and exhibit entanglement. This work presents a systematic study of fundamental concepts, computational mechanisms, and discrete algorithms in quantum computing. The introduction discusses binary bits and qubits, classical logical gates, and their quantum counterparts, highlighting the reversible nature of quantum computation. The materials and methods examine XOR-based classical cryptography, quantum cryptography, quantum teleportation, and mathematical representations of quantum states using probability amplitudes, superposition, and entanglement. The results and discussion focus on the quantum computing model and the implementation of reversible logic through important quantum gates, particularly the Toffoli and Fredkin gates. The role of superposition and entanglement in manipulating quantum information and performing computations is also analyzed. Based on these foundations, the proposed framework emphasizes discrete quantum algorithms for solving problems involving Boolean functions, binary strings, search spaces, integers, graphs, and combinatorial structures. Representative quantum algorithms, including Deutsch, Deutsch–Jozsa, Bernstein–Vazirani, Simon, Grover, and Shor, demonstrate the application of quantum principles to discrete computational problems. The study further explores the relationship between quantum computing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Quantum Machine Learning (QML), where quantum representations and algorithms can support optimization, classification, search, and data-processing tasks. The work concludes by identifying future research directions involving quantum AI, hybrid quantum–classical architectures, error-resilient quantum systems, scalable hardware, and practical discrete quantum algorithms.

items.title: Exploring Magnetic Field Shielding as an Input Sensing Technique
items.abstract: In the field of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), the development of innovative input-sensing methods is a core research endeavor. The availability of various input-sensing methods not only provide alternative ways to address challenges in prototyping caused by resource constraints or methodological intricacies but also facilitate the exploration and development of more intuitive, responsive, and immersive interactions with digital devices. Accordingly, we introduce a new input-sensing approach based on magnetic field shielding (MFS), a phenomenon traditionally used to reduce magnetic interference but largely unexplored as an input sensing mechanism in any form. Our approach exploits the measurable change in magnetic field at a smartphone magnetometer caused by bringing a ferromagnetic shielding element into its sensing region. By treating this shielding-induced change as an input signal, the position or manipulation of the shielding element can be used to enable binary and position-based analog-type interactions. We investigate the theoretical foundations of MFS for input sensing and validate its feasibility through a series of controlled experiments. By detecting changes in magnetometer signals using both rule-based signal processing and machine learning techniques, we demonstrate that MFS can serve as an input-sensing mechanism. Specifically, our experiments support binary and predefined position-based interactions; under participant-held-out evaluation of presegmented candidates, the primary ExtraTrees hierarchy achieved 84.8% balanced accuracy, while the MiniRocket-based comparator achieved 87.6% balanced accuracy. Moreover, we also present an initial exploration of the user experience (with N = 15) afforded by this sensing approach in the context of tangible interaction, evaluating both forms of interaction (binary and position-based analog control) enabled by MFS through application scenarios. The obtained results demonstrate that the prototype achieved more than 95% average interaction success rate across all user trials for both binary and position-based analog-type interactions, while participants reported that the MFS-based tangible controls were easy to manipulate. Finally, we also demonstrate and discuss the utility of the MFS approach through various application scenarios within the interaction contexts evaluated in this work.

items.title: Exploring the Future of Pharmacy Through AI and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: Pharmacy is changing fast thanks to artificial intelligence and a bunch of other technologies—machine learning, deep learning, robotics, big data, IoT, blockchain, and digital health platforms. This review digs into how all these tools are shaking up things like drug discovery, personalized treatments, clinical drug management, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and the supply chain. The focus here is mainly on recent peer-reviewed work, plus a handful of major papers that really stand out.The big takeaways? AI shines brightest in molecular modeling, image-based diagnosis, and tasks where there’s lots of structured data to predict. The evidence isn’t as strong yet for robotics, blockchain, or telepharmacy—there’s hype, but not a ton of proven outcomes. There are some stubborn challenges too: poor data quality, biased models, not enough transparency, patchy regulation, risks to cybersecurity and privacy, and digital systems that aren’t evenly spread out.What does all this mean for pharmacists? Their jobs aren’t going away, but the role will look pretty different. Instead of being replaced, pharmacists need to get good at interpreting what algorithms spit out, keeping a close eye on automated systems, and making sure patient care stays front and center. The review also points out some key gaps and priorities—like making sure new solutions are really validated, deployed fairly, and backed by solid interdisciplinary education.

items.title: Exploring Use of Conversational AI to Investigate Maintenance Problems: Insights from an Early Deployment in a Mining Organisation
items.abstract: Industrial maintenance dashboards make downtime patterns visible, but investigating those patterns requires users to connect records with operational knowledge. We report findings from a preliminary qualitative study where a conversational AI dashboard called Maintenance AI was deployed over a month in a mining organisation. Drawing primarily on interviews and participant feedback, we examine how participants across organisational roles described exploring maintenance information and the use of Maintenance AI. Their accounts suggest that conversational queries greatly helped participants investigate questions arising from dashboard results. We report three overlapping uses of Maintenance AI: comparison with other evidence, consistency testing, and selective checking based on the perceived consequences of an answer. For future conversational maintenance systems, these findings make recommendations around providing data source, time period, and filters behind each answer; explaining missing data and unsupported queries; and supporting evidence checking, question refinement, and correction while preserving query context.
